claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast, as-cast-microstructure state.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
High-temperature yield performance near 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 is a relevant mechanical benchmark for this alloy.
A thin, conformal, high-density alumina layer can be deposited onto cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by a route such as atomic layer deposition or physical vapor deposition.
The deposited alumina coating will improve the alloy's oxygen resistance at high temperature.
The alumina coating will form a continuous and adherent barrier on the cast alloy.
Alumina has sufficiently low oxygen diffusivity under the proposed conditions to impede oxygen ingress.
Alumina is thermodynamically stable at the proposed high-temperature exposure conditions.
Limiting oxygen diffusion through the coating will prevent rapid oxygen uptake by equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina barrier will mitigate or prevent surface pesting during exposure.
The coating will not significantly alter the underlying microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have lower oxidation-induced weight gain than untreated specimens.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have a shallower oxide scale than untreated specimens.
The coating will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility without significant loss relative to untreated material.
The coating will preserve high-temperature yield strength without significant loss relative to untreated material.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers pesting and oxidation during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
The predicted protection is limited to temperatures around 800 °C and exposure durations of approximately 5 hours.
The predicted preservation of mechanical performance applies to loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 and may not extend to more extreme loading.
